---
name: odk-readiness-check
description: Assess project readiness and prepare approved AI-guidance and documentation updates
---

This is a core ODK command and is available even when no optional modules are enabled. It enters through the ODK orchestrator.

1. Read `.opendevkit/workflows/readiness-refactor.md`.
2. Delegate evidence review and readiness classification to the internal Readiness specialist.
3. Before optional-module questions, inspect `.opendevkit/config.json` and treat a missing `preferences.optionalModulesSetup` as `"pending"`.
4. Ask about optional modules only when setup is pending or the user explicitly requests module changes. Present modules one at a time in authoritative catalog order using “Would you like to enable the `<module>` module?” with “Yes” / “No” choices. After each “Yes,” resolve and ask only that module install guide's unanswered setup questions immediately, before asking about the next module; if none remain, proceed without an extra interview. All “No” answers form a valid empty selection. For another workspace, confirm it before preparing setup. Do not re-ask completed setup.
5. Use the core-installed catalog for recorded provenance or the resolved commit's catalog for legacy setup. After selection, load only selected modules' manifests and install guides as setup inputs, or none for an empty selection. Follow the canonical workflow for mappings, prerequisites, questions, and checks. Ask only unanswered module-specific decisions that can affect setup; if none remain, do not add an interview.
6. With valid recorded `source.repository` and full commit SHA in `source.commit`, Readiness fetches every selected manifest source read-only from that exact repository and commit. Never substitute a branch, tag, latest revision, abbreviated SHA, or another repository even on retrieval failure. If source provenance is entirely absent, resolve the canonical ODK repository's latest default-branch commit once and retrieve the complete core source set and selected module sources from that single immutable SHA, even for an empty selection. If a `source` record is present but incomplete or malformed, stop and report it instead of replacing possibly custom or conflicting provenance. Unselected lightweight metadata is retrieved only as core refresh material. If resolution fails or any required source or mapping cannot be retrieved or validated, stop and report; do not prepare a partial plan or write.
7. Inspect all core, module and configuration destinations, preflight safety and stage content without changing project targets. Present one consolidated exact plan naming the source repository and commit, each manifest destination, the complete proposed contents or diff for every destination, answers and their effects, configuration changes, and checks. Identify each conflict and include exact conditional config changes and skipped targets for decline outcomes and incomplete modules. For legacy setup include all ODK-managed core targets and proposed contents or diffs and a safely merged config; exclude unrelated project files. Build the preview only after all required files are retrieved and validated. If any proposed material cannot be determined, report the blocker rather than present an incomplete plan as exact. Retrieval and preview are read-only. Obtain explicit approval of the exact plan, then a separate replacement decision for every conflicting target before any write. Recheck all destinations; if changed or unsafe, stop before writes and obtain approval of a revised plan and any new conflict decisions. Recheck each target immediately before writing; if it changes after writes begin, stop the affected work and report the partial state.
8. Apply only staged, approved material. If any module replacement is declined, leave every target of that module unchanged and do not enable it; other independently approved modules may proceed only if safe and covered by the plan. If the plan is declined or a required core replacement is unapproved, leave existing core and module files and configuration unchanged and setup pending; do not apply the legacy refresh or install selected modules. Pending describes the unfinished request in this case; report the actual unchanged config marker. For legacy refresh, finish and verify every required core target before installing modules or recording `source.repository` and `source.commit`. Verify all module targets before enabling only fully installed modules in `enabledModules`; set `preferences.optionalModulesSetup: "configured"` only when the approved selection is complete, including an empty list for no modules, otherwise keep it pending. Preserve unrelated configuration.
9. On a core write or verification failure, stop the refresh and module installation without recording new provenance. On a module failure, stop that module and do not enable it; keep setup pending if the approved config can safely be written. Other independently approved modules may proceed only if safe. Partial writes are not a conflict-decline skip or guaranteed rollback. Report exactly changed, failed and unattempted files and actual configuration and provenance state; if the config write fails, do not claim the intended state was recorded or use a success-shaped fallback. Module data operations require their own applicable explicit choices and proposed-change approvals; module selection or installation alone does not authorize them.
10. Check workspace `.vscode/settings.json` for `chat.defaultConfiguration.approvals === "allowAll"` before offering it. Do not offer it again when already enabled. If disabled or absent, ask before changing only that workspace setting. Preserve JSONC/comments/unrelated settings, make no user-level change or bypass, and report trust or policy restrictions.
11. Ask the user only about unresolved readiness topics reported by Readiness.
12. Have Readiness prepare one consolidated documentation preview after clarification.
13. Present the preview and wait for approval before applying any proposed documentation changes.

For each newly selected module, invoke its manifest-declared optional `readinessWorkflow` only after successful installation, verification, and enablement. Also invoke declared readiness workflows for already-enabled modules. Do not dispatch for declined, unselected, skipped, or incompletely installed modules; skip the hook when an enabled module has no declaration. Module workflows return findings and unresolved questions to ODK; they do not communicate with the user or authorize writes.

Ask each unresolved readiness decision as one focused question with concise, closed, evidence-based choices. Do not require a free-form explanation or repeat a decision established by evidence or prior user input. Use selected module install-guide choices for module setup questions. Follow the canonical workflow's exact built-in prompts and applicability conditions: setup plan (“Do you approve this exact setup plan?” — “Approve” / “Decline”); each conflicting path (“Replace the existing file at `<path>` with the proposed content?” — “Replace” / “Keep existing”); documentation (“Do you approve the proposed documentation changes?” — “Approve all” / “Approve selected files” / “Decline”); workspace Allow All when not already enabled (“Enable Allow All approvals for this workspace?” — “Enable” / “Leave unchanged”); and missing OpenSpec tooling (“Would you like me to prepare a project-scoped OpenSpec setup plan for this workspace?” — “Yes” / “No”). Keep all approvals distinct from clarification answers and from one another.

Readiness returns findings and proposed changes only to ODK. It does not communicate directly with the user or modify implementation code.
